# Playbook for hx_picket_channel

When hiding, avoid predictable center cells. Choose edge or near-edge positions (1-3 or 7-9) since opponents will likely cluster in the middle. Vary your pattern across rounds to prevent exploitation. Once you commit to a specific cell in a mutual escort agreement, honor that commitment exactly—deviations break trust and forfeit points.

When posting station notes, keep them brief and action-oriented. Use notes for specific tactical proposals: exact cell commitments for mutual escort trades, observed hiding patterns, or direct responses to other boats' claims. Avoid vague statements about cooperation that consume note budget without substance.

When firing under standing orders, choose your target cell deliberately based on available information. Track each opponent's hiding patterns across rounds and look for tendencies (e.g., preference for edge cells, clustering in specific ranges). Build a mental map of each boat's behavior over time. If no clear pattern exists yet, spread fire across different cells rather than repeating arbitrary coordinates.

When claiming hit or miss, always match the office's private result exactly. This is mandatory and non-negotiable—honor the game's truth-telling mechanism. Never deviate from what the office told you privately.

When making escort claims, track through each round which boats have mutual escort opportunities with you. Only claim escort for a round if both you and the target boat have explicitly named each other in their station notes before the claim stage. Do not assume mutual escort—verify bilateral confirmation. When a boat refuses to pre-commit to a specific cell due to timing constraints (the standing order means they fire before they know where you hide), accept their position gracefully rather than creating unnecessary friction. Some mutual escort pairings are possible; others are not given the turn structure.

When negotiating mutual escort trades in station notes, demand specificity with boats that can deliver it. Push for exact cell commitments before the round in which you will escort. If a boat explains they cannot pre-commit due to standing order timing (e.g., they fire before you hide), do not interpret this as bad faith—acknowledge their constraint and shift to partnerships with boats for whom mutual commitment is feasible.

Establish mutual escort relationships with boats that reciprocate clearly and keep their word. Prioritize reliable partners and reinforce stability in notes. When a mutual escort agreement is locked (both boats named in prior rounds), carry it through to completion and claim the points confidently.

In the final round, continue following standing orders and the patterns that have worked. Do not abandon established strategy. A final-round departure from your approach wastes your last shot.

Do not fire on Harbor. The payoff threat (3 points to Harbor, 3 to you on any shot) is a credible deterrent and damages your reputation with other boats. Harbor's threat to "put you off the board" costs you all future shots, which is far worse than any immediate payoff.

Track the standing fire order (Echo → Foxtrot → Gamma → Echo) and know when you will shoot next. Use this to plan your hiding strategy and understand which boats can realistically lock mutual escort with you given the timing of when they shoot relative to when they hide.

Revise mutual escort targets as evidence accumulates. Some boats will prove reliable; others will show they cannot or will not pre-commit. After a boat has declined pre-commitment multiple times with clear reasoning, stop pushing them and redirect your escort efforts toward boats with whom mutual agreement is achievable.

# Foxtrot's Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hide Strategy
When choosing where to hide, pick a middle-range cell (4-6) rather than extremes or the dead center. Avoid being predictable. Cell 5 is a reliable default that balances centrality with flexibility.

## Note Strategy
When other boats propose open coordination and transparency, acknowledge it but do not commit to revealing your actual strategy in advance. Use notes to signal cooperative intent without binding yourself operationally. Mirror the language of cooperation without surrendering tactical flexibility.

When pressed for specific commitments, offer bounded alternatives—e.g., "I will choose from cells X or Y and announce after Round N resolves"—rather than naming a single cell now. This maintains credibility while preserving decision-making room based on actual board state.

Do not commit to specific hide cells in notes before the hide stage of that round arrives. Even if other boats demand it to guarantee mutual escort payoff, the execution risk of pre-committing outweighs the 5-point escort gain.

As the game progresses and some boats lock mutual escort pacts with each other, acknowledge their success cleanly and respectfully in notes. Do not attempt to join pacts mid-game if you cannot credibly commit to their mechanics. Signal that you are playing your own independent game without resentment. This closes coordination channels professionally and avoids creating enemies in the final rounds.

## Fire Strategy
When the standing order tells me to fire at a specific boat, fire at that boat. Do not deviate from standing orders based on speculation about coordination or pressure from other boats.

When firing, choose a cell that is not the boat's most obvious position but also not random—aim for cells in the 4-6 range where boats often hide. This is where boats naturally cluster when trying to balance safety with tactical flexibility.

## Claim Strategy
When the office tells me privately whether my shot hit or missed, claim that truth. Do not lie about results. Integrity preserves your reputation for the remaining rounds and your final score. A single lie discovered destroys trust permanently.

## Escort Strategy
When the escort stage arrives, name another boat only if you have actual information that you escorted them that round—meaning you know where they hid and can verify they were there. If you have no basis for an escort claim, claim none rather than guessing.

Do not name a boat as escort unless you can justify it with real observation. Even if you coordinated to do so, if you don't have solid information, it's safer to claim none. Do not attempt to claim escort with boats that have locked mutual escort pacts with other boats—those pacts are closed loops, and inserting yourself into them after they're established will fail and damage your credibility.

## Overall Approach
Separate your public signals (notes) from your actual moves (hide, fire, claim). You can sound cooperative in notes while playing competitively in action. Stick to standing orders. Tell the truth about shot results. Do not make escort claims without real information. 

Build a reputation for truthfulness about outcomes, tactical flexibility about future moves, and respectful acknowledgment of other boats' pacts and strategies. Accept that in a multi-player game with locked alliances, your best play may be honest independence rather than forcing yourself into coalitions that don't suit your mechanics or timing constraints.

# Playbook for hx_picket_channel

**On hiding:** Place yourself in central cells (4-6) rather than extremes. This balances defensive positioning against predictability without overcommitting to any sector.

**On station notes:** Match the communication tenor of the table. When others propose coordination, acknowledge it openly while maintaining realistic skepticism about competitive incentives. Signal that you evaluate proposals on merit, not blind alliance. Move quickly from signaling openness to proposing concrete, specific deals—cell commitments, round ranges, mutual names. Vague willingness to "coordinate" leaves value on the table. Lock escort pacts by round 3 at the latest; post-round-4 offers arrive too late for credible mutual commitment since players cannot plan future hides with confidence.

**On firing:** When you have a standing target, commit to it. Don't second-guess the duty rotation—it exists to prevent collusion spirals. Fire at cells where the target is likely to be based on their previous positions and behavior patterns. Even in the final round, executing your standing duty preserves the norm that makes cooperation possible in future games. A locked mutual escort pact does not override the standing order; you fire on schedule and claim truthfully. The pact governs the escort stage, not the fire stage.

**On shot claims:** Always claim truthfully what the office tells you. Lying to gain a single-round advantage costs more in credibility than it gains in points, especially when other players will learn your deception and adjust their cooperation offers downward.

**On escort claims:** Before the escort stage, track which boats have been acting cooperatively with you and have made explicit, specific commitments. A mutual escort pact locked by name and cell and round in an earlier note stage is a real deal—execute it in the escort stage even if you missed your shot that round or fired on that boat per standing order. The fire stage and escort stage are independent domains. Do not claim an escort with a boat you have not formalized an agreement with, even if they signaled general openness. Specificity is the difference between intention and commitment.

**What worked this episode:** Locked a two-round mutual escort pact with Echo (rounds 5-6, cell 5) by proposing concrete terms early and getting explicit reciprocal confirmation. Executed it in round 5 when Echo was at cell 5 and secured the 5-point mutual gain. Held the pact in round 6 by claiming escort on Echo even though I fired on Echo per standing order and the shot missed. Stayed truthful on all fire claims. Ended at +20.0.

**What still didn't work:** Failed to close a similar pact with Foxtrot despite their repeated good-faith offers. Requested explicit cell commitments too late (round 5) when Foxtrot could not credibly lock a round 6 plan. Left mutual 5-point gains on the table by not settling terms by round 3 or 4.

**Next time:** Propose concrete, specific escort deals by round 3 at the latest—name the other boat, name the cells, name the rounds, all in your station note. Get explicit reciprocal confirmation in their next note. Lock at least two mutual pacts before the midpoint. Understand that a locked escort pact is independent of fire duty; you still fire on your standing target and claim truthfully, but you execute the escort claim in the salvage stage if you had formalized the agreement. Do not treat post-round-4 coordination offers as actionable; by then the timing window for credible commitment is closing. When you have locked pacts, execute them faithfully in the escort stage even if circumstances shift on the fire stage. That reliability is how you secure the second and third pacts.
